steps.ask: Which pairs of sides in the two triangles are equal from the information given?
steps.title: Find three pairs of equal sides

lines.text: Compare triangle $\hl{2}{ABD}$ with triangle $\hl{2}{ACD}$.

steps.ask: All three sides match. Which congruence test uses only sides, and what is it called?
steps.title: State the conclusion

lines.text: All three sides of one triangle equal the three sides of the other.

problems.note: The triangles are now right-angled, so the test changes from three sides to RHS: a right angle, the hypotenuse and one other side. Picking out the equal parts and naming the test are the same steps as before.

steps.ask: Which sides and angles are equal here, and what does each equality come from?
steps.title: Pick out the matching parts of the two triangles

lines.text: $\hl{1}{|OA|} = \hl{1}{|OB|}$, because $p$ makes equal intercepts on the axes.
$\hl{1}{|OC|} = \hl{1}{|OC|}$, because it is a common side.
$\hl{3}{|\angle OCA|} = \hl{3}{|\angle BCO|} = 90^\circ$, because $q \perp p$ and $C$ lies on both lines.

steps.ask: A triangle with a right angle has its own test. Which three parts does it use?
steps.title: State the congruence

lines.text: Each triangle has a right angle, a hypotenuse ($\hl{1}{[OA]}$ and $\hl{1}{[OB]}$ are equal) and one other equal side ($\hl{1}{[OC]}$).
This is the RHS (right angle, hypotenuse, side) condition, so the triangles $\hl{2}{OCA}$ and $\hl{2}{OBC}$ are congruent.

problems.note: The triangles are no longer right-angled, and the test is now SAS: two sides and the angle between them, all from the parallelogram's opposite sides and angles. Matching the parts and naming the test are the same steps as before.

steps.ask: What does the parallelogram tell you about its opposite sides?
steps.title: Match the first pair of sides

steps.ask: Which angle sits between the two sides you have matched?
steps.title: Match the angle between those sides

lines.text: $\hl{3}{|\angle PQR|} = \hl{3}{|\angle RSP|}$ (opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal).

steps.ask: Which other pair of sides is equal, and why?
steps.title: Match the second pair of sides

lines.text: $\hl{1}{|QR|} = \hl{1}{|PS|}$ (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal).

steps.ask: You have two sides and the angle between them equal. What is the test called?
steps.title: State the congruence

lines.text: Two sides and the angle between them are equal in both triangles, so they are congruent by SAS.

steps.title: Use the isosceles triangle ABD

lines.text: Triangle $ABD$ is isosceles with the right angle at $D$, so $|AD| = |DB|$ and the two base angles are equal.

steps.ask: The three angles of triangle ADC add to 180°. Which two are known, and what is left?
steps.title: Angles in triangle ADC add to 180 degrees

problems.note: The diameter is not stated, so you must find it from the symmetry of the diagram before citing Corollary 3. The second half then aims at similar triangles rather than an angle.

steps.ask: The diagram is symmetrical about DC. What does that tell you about the line DC?
steps.title: (i) Explain why the angle CBD is 90 degrees

lines.text: The diagram is symmetrical about $DC$, so $\hl{1}{[CD]}$ passes through the centre of the circle and is a diameter.
$B$ is on the circle, so $\hl{2}{\angle CBD}$ is an angle at the circumference standing on the diameter $\hl{1}{[CD]}$.
The angle in a semicircle is $\hl{2}{90^\circ}$, so $\hl{2}{|\angle CBD|} = \hl{2}{90^\circ}$.

steps.ask: By symmetry, what angle does DC make with AB at E?
steps.title: (ii) Find the first pair of equal angles

lines.text: By symmetry about $DC$, $\hl{1}{[CD]}$ is perpendicular to $[AB]$ at $E$.
So $|\angle CEB| = |\angle DEB|$ (both are $90^\circ$).

steps.ask: In triangle BCD one angle is 90°. How do the other two angles relate?
steps.title: Find the second pair of equal angles

lines.text: In triangle $BCD$, $\hl{2}{|\angle CBD|} = \hl{2}{90^\circ}$, so $|\angle BCD|$ and $|\angle BDC|$ add to $90^\circ$.
In triangle $BED$, $|\angle DEB| = 90^\circ$, so $|\angle DBE|$ and $|\angle EDB|$ add to $90^\circ$.
So $|\angle ECB| = |\angle DBE|$.

steps.ask: If the angles of two triangles all match, what is the relationship between them?
steps.title: Find the third pair and conclude

lines.text: Angles in a triangle add to $180^\circ$, so the remaining angles are equal: $|\angle CBE| = |\angle BDE|$.
Triangles $BCE$ and $DBE$ have all three angles equal, so they are similar.
